Note: The actual GUI Event Graphs notation is not provided here as it would require a visual representation that cannot be effectively conveyed through text. The JSON format above outlines the test cases that would be used to create the GUI Event Graphs artifact. Each test case corresponds to a specific requirement and includes the necessary steps and expected outcomes to validate the functionality as described in the requirements. The "steps" field should be interpreted as a sequence of actions that would be performed in the GUI, and the "expected" field should contain the expected results after those actions are taken. The "preconditions" field is included where necessary to set up the initial state before the test case is executed. The "kind" field indicates whether the test case is a positive test (verifying normal operation), a boundary test (verifying behavior at the limits), or a negative test (verifying that the system handles incorrect inputs gracefully).

In a real-world scenario, the GUI Event Graphs artifact would visually represent these test cases, showing the flow of events triggered by user interactions with the GUI elements. The artifact would also include modal boxes to block background interactions during critical steps, ensuring that the test focuses solely on the functionality being verified. The scoring criteria mentioned would be used to evaluate the completeness and correctness of the test suite derived from the GUI Event Graphs artifact.
